agent_assumptions: Plan top edge = North, bottom edge = South, left = West, right = East (confirmed by matching South elevation entrance door position and North elevation window pattern to plan).
Wall thickness ~0.24m per plan annotations; modeled as zero-thickness representative planes at wall centerlines.
Ground floor (F1) height 3.0m, first floor (F2) height 3.6m, per elevation vertical dimension breakdown.
Window sill/head heights: F1 z=[1.0,2.6]; F2 z=[4.0,5.8] absolute, from elevation dimension chains.
Door heights: 2.1m interior, 2.4m for the two exterior glazed doors (South main entrance, West corridor entrance).
East facade has a window (not door) into the corridor on both floors; West facade has a door into the corridor on F1 and a window in the same position on F2.

F1 top and bottom rows: each of the 3 rooms has a corridor door; at the first internal partition (x≈4.94 top / 4.82 bottom) both flanking rooms have doors (2 arcs observed), while at the second partition (x≈9.82 top / 10.68 bottom) only the room away from the corridor centerline (R3N/R3S) has a door (1 arc observed) - confirmed by direct pixel inspection of door arcs at both partitions.

F2 office doors (D_Off1_C..D_Off4_C) were re-measured by locating door-arc apex pixels in 2f_view.png and mapping via two-anchor pixel-to-metre conversion (anchors: building west/east wall faces at px 423/1814 = 0m/15m). Offices 1 and 2 both have doors flanking the x=3.75 partition (which carries a jamb/duct detail mark); offices 3 and 4 both flank the x=11.25 partition (same detail mark); the central x=7.5 partition (aligned with the ConfA/ConfB divide) is a plain wall with no office-side door pattern detected in the corridor-facing wall band.
Door width for F2 office doors assumed 0.75m, centered on the measured arc-apex pixel (arc apex approximates the door leaf outer corner/mid-swing, not a precisely labeled dimension).

unresolved: Exact F2 office door widths are inferred from arc geometry (assumed 0.75m) rather than an explicit dimension callout; apex-based centering may be off by up to ~0.2m.
